f66_01_ledger_custody_transfer.approval_ref: StegVerse-org/.github#98 RESPONSE-067 (6082533976) F66-01; RESPONSE-069 (6082671705) F69-01; RESPONSE-071 (6082871031) F71-02; RESPONSE-073 (6083095827) F71-02 correction
f66_01_ledger_custody_transfer.question: Can a relocated Organization ledger root be told apart from a copied one, so two copies cannot each advance and fork Organization reality?
f66_01_ledger_custody_transfer.design: Every Organization receipt carries custody_generation (resident-runtime/aggregate_repo_transition.py:891); a receipt without the field predates custody transfer and is generation 0 (resident-runtime/aggregate_repo_transition.py:154), so existing chains verify unchanged and no history is rewritten. ORGANIZATION_LEDGER_CUSTODY_RELEASED (release_custody, resident-runtime/aggregate_repo_transition.py:716) is a manifest-bound Organization transition appended under ORGANIZATION_LEDGER_LOCK by the existing emitter _aggregate_transition_locked; the governing manifest's ledger_custody_transfer declares successor_materialization_id, predecessor_head_sha256 and next_custody_generation, and the receipt binds them with the manifest digest. Once it is HEAD every further append and batch closure on that root is CUSTODY_RELEASED_ROOT_IS_READ_ONLY FAIL_CLOSED (resident-runtime/aggregate_repo_transition.py:389; resident-runtime/organization_batch_custody.py:797). ORGANIZATION_LEDGER_CUSTODY_ASSUMED (assume_custody, resident-runtime/aggregate_repo_transition.py:746) is the first append permitted at the successor; it reads the release back through the existing HEAD check, chain walk and verified_organization_receipt and requires the release to name this successor_materialization_id, the manifest's predecessor HEAD (equal to the release's own predecessor) and next generation, and the same manifest. A missing release, a wrong successor, a mismatched HEAD or generation, and an interrupted handover (release receipt durable, HEAD not advanced) are typed FAIL_CLOSED refusals naming a retry entrypoint; the exact release retried completes an interrupted HEAD without a second receipt.
f66_01_ledger_custody_transfer.exclusivity_limit: A5 limit, open: the .append.lock fcntl lock serializes writers within one kernel only, and no shared serializer, CAS, lock service or store is added. A copy of a root taken before its release can still be written on another node; source cannot prevent that. It is detected and refused FAIL_CLOSED wherever its receipts meet the release or each other: verify_custody_lineage (resident-runtime/aggregate_repo_transition.py:192), run by every append, verified_organization_receipt, the HEAD/chain walk (_segment), verify_batch and close_batch (resident-runtime/organization_batch_custody.py:182,314,352,794), refuses CUSTODY_GENERATION_SUPERSEDED for a receipt in a generation a recorded release or assumption closed that is not an ancestor of it, and ORGANIZATION_CUSTODY_FORK_DETECTED for two receipts naming one predecessor. A stale copy that never meets the release verifies on its own. Nothing reports a safe transfer.
f66_01_ledger_custody_transfer.kept_open: EXISTING_PRIVATE_ORGANIZATION_LEDGER_ROOT_REACHABLE_AT_MANIFEST_DIRECTED_INVOCATION (current_truth.local_batch_runtime_proof): source conformance does not prove the root is reachable at runtime; cross-kernel prevention of a pre-release copy writing remains an open A5 limit.
f66_01_ledger_custody_transfer.f69_01_successor_exclusivity_gate: Detection is not exclusivity. Once a root's HEAD is in custody_generation >= 1, every consequential write other than the ORGANIZATION_LEDGER_CUSTODY_ASSUMED record itself (an append, a manifest-directed packet release, a batch closure, a further release) is CUSTODY_EXCLUSIVITY_UNAUTHENTICATED FAIL_CLOSED with retry entrypoint resident-runtime/aggregate_repo_transition.py::aggregate_transition (require_custody_exclusivity, resident-runtime/aggregate_repo_transition.py:291, checked before any packet release at :640 and at resident-runtime/organization_batch_custody.py:800), unless the injected custody_exclusivity_verifier returns an attestation of unique custody binding the exact successor_materialization_id, custody_generation, current predecessor HEAD and the exact action (custody_action_sha256 over the org_transition_class and the source transition digest, or the closure reason for a batch closure); an attestation for another HEAD or action or already bound in a receipt is a replay and refused; a verifier that raises is FAIL_CLOSED. Its digest is bound in the receipt. There is no default and no environment fallback. custody_exclusivity is a limitation field, never a passing predicate.
f66_01_ledger_custody_transfer.existing_exclusivity_authority: NONE wired: no existing authority in this repository attests unique custody of a successor_materialization_id and custody_generation, so none is injected and a successor makes no consequential append. resident-runtime/ledger_store.py PosixLedgerStore serializes by the kernel-local .append.lock only. resident-runtime/ledger_store.py GitLedgerStore (#3060) serializes appends to its ref by kernel-local git update-ref compare-and-swap on its own git_dir only; after F75-01 no remote CAS gates an append, so it serializes nothing across kernels and attests ref-append serialization within one kernel, not custody of a materialization, and was not wired.
f66_01_ledger_custody_transfer.f71_02_ungoverned_relocation: The generation-0 exemption is not portable by copying. The location check is anomaly detection only, never custody authority: a matching location proves neither identity nor authority. A consequential write (any append but ASSUMED, a packet release, a batch closure, a release) requires the supplied root to be the location HEAD.json's absolute receipt_path records (require_no_relocation_anomaly, resident-runtime/aggregate_repo_transition.py:347); otherwise, with no RELEASED/ASSUMED handover having moved it, it is UNGOVERNED_RELOCATION_ANOMALY_DETECTED FAIL_CLOSED with retry entrypoint resident-runtime/aggregate_repo_transition.py::release_custody. Reads and verification compare only the root-relative locator, so #3057's readback portability is kept. Relocation is only RELEASED/ASSUMED plus the F69-01 verifier. Limit: a byte copy at the identical absolute path on another kernel cannot be distinguished; it is covered only by fork and superseded-generation detection (DETECTED_NOT_PREVENTED_ACROSS_KERNELS). On a GitLedgerStore (#3060) the recorded location is the ref locator, never a host path, so a Git ledger materialized into another git_dir with the same ref is not distinguished by this check; after F75-01 appends are serialized only by the kernel-local update-ref CAS, and two nodes that append to one ref are detected as ORGANIZATION_LEDGER_FORK_DETECTED at propagation (DETECTED_NOT_PREVENTED_ACROSS_KERNELS), not serialized.
f66_01_ledger_custody_transfer.custody_authority_basis: Every generation-0 receipt records custody_authority_basis = "PRE_EXISTING_MATERIALIZATION_UNAUTHENTICATED; LOCATION_CHECK_IS_ANOMALY_DETECTION_ONLY" (resident-runtime/aggregate_repo_transition.py:120,894): the materialization that writes generation 0 is not authenticated by anything in source.
f66_01_ledger_custody_transfer.cross_kernel_prevention_tested: NONE: no test establishes cross-kernel prevention; tests establish detection and fail-closed refusal only.

q74_01_bounded_a.design: resident-runtime/organization_batch_custody.py::readback_custody_basis reports a verified readback's custody basis: a generation-0 receipt's own custody_authority_basis (PRE_EXISTING_MATERIALIZATION_UNAUTHENTICATED; LOCATION_CHECK_IS_ANOMALY_DETECTION_ONLY), a fail-closed value when a generation-0 row lacks it, and DETECTED_NOT_PREVENTED_ACROSS_KERNELS; NO_CUSTODY_AUTHORITY_CLAIMED for a handover generation. Every non-legacy consumer that reports a verified Organization readback carries organization_readback_custody_basis beside it (claim allocator, custody readback, KV publisher return, canonical organization_receipt_gate, manifest InTr ingress, SDK diagnostic consumer, orphan recovery, functional memory).
q74_01_bounded_a.unchanged: Receipt bodies and hashes, accept/refuse behavior and historical readback are unchanged; no new authority and no new dependency.

f75_01_remote_cas_isolated.design: resident-runtime/ledger_store.py GitLedgerStore appends and reads only its local git_dir ref; exclusive/append_transaction/publish/get/list_prefix never read or write the remote, and publication is the kernel-local git update-ref <ref> <new> <old> CAS, so transition completion never awaits a remote. The remote is reached only by two explicit steps outside every transition: materialize (seed or fast-forward the local ref before invocation) and propagate (after a completed local append; push --force-with-lease naming the observed remote tip, which must be an ancestor of the local tip, so fast-forward only, never rewrite). propagate returns a non-gating disposition: PROPAGATED (also on an exact retry), FAIL_CLOSED ORGANIZATION_LEDGER_REMOTE_UNREACHABLE or ORGANIZATION_LEDGER_REMOTE_PUBLISH_UNCONFIRMED with retry_entrypoint resident-runtime/ledger_store.py::GitLedgerStore.propagate, or FAIL_CLOSED ORGANIZATION_LEDGER_FORK_DETECTED for a divergence (detected, not prevented). It never waits or retries and never undoes the local append. No transition invokes it; if propagation is not admitted it is not invoked.
f75_01_remote_cas_isolated.unchanged: PosixLedgerStore, receipt/batch formats and hashes, and the local lost-race FAIL_CLOSED are unchanged; no new store, machine, networked lock, framework or dependency.

items.E1-r1: A broken HEAD-reachable chain returns typed FAIL_CLOSED REPO_LEDGER_CHAIN_BREAK; no receipt is minted after a missing mid-chain node.
items.E1-r2: Inventory every state-transition caller of the emitter and require the exact-retry idempotence policy appropriate to each state-effect action.
items.E1-r4: Exact retry compares predecessor_state_sha256, successor_state_sha256, authority_effect and all identity-defining evidence; divergent identity is a collision, never a returned prior receipt.
items.E1-r5: Every node visited by recorded() has its receipt digest recomputed with the existing digest helper and compared with its key and stored receipt_sha256; a malformed or corrupted node fails closed as REPO_LEDGER_CHAIN_BREAK.
